Caikitāneya (‘descendant of Cekitāna’) is mentioned as a
teacher in the Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa.^1 The Caikitā-
neyas are also referred to there^2 in connexion with the Sāman
which they worshipped. Brahmadatta Caikitāneya is brought
into connexion with the Sāman in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad.^3
and Vāsiṣṭha Caikitāneya is known to the Ṣaḍviṃśa^4 and
Vaṃśa Brāhmaṇas.^5 The word is a patronymic, formed from
[]
Caikitāna, according to Śaṅkara,^6 but more probably from
Cekitāna,^7 a name found in the Epic.
1) i. 37, 7; ii. 5, 2.
2) i. 42, 1.
3) i. 3, 24.
4) iv. 1.
5) Indische Studien, 4, 373, 384.
6) On Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad,
loc. cit.
7) St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.

Caikitāyana, ‘descendant of Cikitāyana^1 or Cekita,’^2 is the
patronymic of Dālbhya in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad.^3
1) Śaṅkara on Chāndogya Upaniṣad,
i. 8, 1.
